task: Stabilize the flaky worker pool test suite
title: Fix data race between goroutines writing to a shared job map
brief: workerpool.go's results map is written from multiple worker goroutines without a lock, and read concurrently from pool_test.go's assertions, causing `go test -race ./workerpool/...` to fail intermittently (about 1 in 20 runs). Diagnose the exact interleaving from the race detector output, then fix it in workerpool.go without serializing the workers (a plain mutex around every write would defeat the pool's purpose) — a sync.Map or sharded-lock approach across both workerpool.go and pool_test.go's setup. Done when `go test -race ./workerpool/... -count=50` is clean.
why: diagnosing and fixing a genuine data race with a performance constraint, unclear until the race trace is read

task: Fix corrupted inventory counts under concurrent checkouts
title: Fix inventory decrement race during checkout
brief: inventory/stock.py's decrement(sku, qty) reads the current count then writes it back without any locking or atomic operation; under concurrent checkouts for the same SKU, decrements are lost (confirmed in the incident report, two customers oversold). Fix using a row-level lock or an atomic SQL decrement with a check constraint across the checkout flow; the retry/backoff behavior on lock contention needs deciding. Done when the load test in tests/inventory/test_concurrent_decrement.py showing 500 concurrent decrements against qty=100 never goes negative.

previous_attempt.outcome: checker FAIL: added a Python-level threading.Lock, which doesn't help across separate worker processes — counts still went negative under the real multi-process load test

why: prior attempt missed the cross-process concurrency reality — one level up from the failed attempt, and the underlying issue is concurrency correctness anyway

task: Stop the payment webhook from double-charging
title: Make the payment webhook handler idempotent
brief: payments/webhook.go processes Stripe webhook retries as new charges when the provider redelivers the same event (network blip on our side, confirmed by two duplicate-charge tickets). Add idempotency keyed on the event ID, safe when two redeliveries arrive at nearly the same time on different instances behind the load balancer — a naive check-then-insert has the same race the current code has, so it needs a real unique constraint or a distributed lock. Done when tests/payments/webhook_concurrent_test.go firing two identical events simultaneously results in exactly one charge.

previous_attempt.outcome: checker FAIL: added an in-memory seen-events set, which doesn't survive across the two running instances — duplicate charge still reproduced by the concurrent test

why: prior fix ignored the multi-instance race that caused the bug in the first place — one level up, and the fix itself is concurrency-correctness work

task: Reduce lock contention in the session store without breaking correctness
title: Small refactor of the session cache's locking
brief: cache/session.go currently holds one global mutex around the entire session map, which is a bottleneck under load. Refactor it to a sharded-lock map (16 shards by key hash), keeping identical read/write semantics for every caller. Must not introduce any window where a session read sees a partially-written value during a concurrent write, and the shard count and hashing scheme need choosing. Done when the existing session tests pass under -race and a new benchmark shows reduced contention.
why: framed as a small refactor, but changing shared-state locking without breaking concurrent-read/write correctness is the concurrency clause, not a pattern-following change

task: Clear a quick item off the backlog before the sprint ends
title: Quick tweak to the auth token refresh
brief: auth/refresh.ts currently refreshes the access token on a plain setTimeout per tab; when a user has the app open in three tabs, all three race to refresh simultaneously, each invalidating the others' new token and occasionally logging the user out mid-session (support ticket volume up since the last release). Needs cross-tab coordination (a BroadcastChannel-based lock or single-leader election among tabs) so exactly one tab refreshes and the others wait for and reuse its result, without introducing a stall if the leader tab closes mid-refresh. Done when a new test in auth/refresh.test.ts simulating three concurrent tabs shows exactly one network refresh call.
why: title reads like a trivial tweak but the brief is cross-tab concurrency coordination with an unclear leader-failure edge case — the concurrency and unclear-edge-case clauses decide, not the title
